title: Scope of works for a service site
audience: Supervisors and owners who write the scope for a service contract at a commercial or office site, and the work instructions for each area.
learningOutcomes: Write a scope of works that lists areas, tasks, frequencies, standards, responsibilities and exclusions
Use frequency language that a client and a team can both check
Select products by surface compatibility, and state the source of that check

instruction.heading: What a scope of works does
instruction.body: A scope of works sets out what work will be done, where, how often, to what standard, by whom, and what is excluded. The price and the rostered hours rest on it. The sample proposal uses a scope with clearly separated areas, tasks and frequencies, and it attaches reporting forms to the same contract. Write yours so that a new team member and the client's site manager would reach the same understanding of the job.

instruction.heading: Divide the site into areas
instruction.body: The sample proposal groups the site into general floors, restrooms, locker rooms and windows. Each area then has its own task list. Walk the site before you write the scope, and draw a simple zone map. Label each area, note its surfaces and fittings, and record who uses it and how often. A scope written from an office floor plan, without a walk, is a common reason for underpriced work.

instruction.heading: Use frequency language that can be checked
instruction.body: The sample uses daily, once per shift, weekly, monthly, quarterly and semi-annual frequencies. These are useful because each can be checked against a record. The frequencies are sample values from a janitorial contract, written for an undated, non-Australian site, so they are not an industry standard. Define each term once in the scope. Write 'once per shift' only after the shift is defined. Avoid 'as required' or 'when needed', because no one can check completion against them. Where a task depends on a trigger such as a spill or a complaint, write the trigger and the response time.

instruction.heading: Standard work instructions at the point of work
instruction.body: The sample plan posts a step-by-step work instruction on the back of the restroom door, with a schedule for initials. This is good practice, because the instruction sits where the work happens. A standard work instruction is a short numbered sheet for one task or one area. It lists the materials, the PPE, the steps, the standard and a sign-off grid. Keep each sheet short, date it and give it a version number. Remove superseded versions from the site.

instruction.heading: Surfaces, chemicals and compatibility
instruction.body: The sample proposal warns against using an acid-based cleaner on stainless steel. The principle applies generally. Each surface tolerates only some products, and some products damage or discolour surfaces or create hazards when mixed. Before a product goes into a scope, check the product label, its safety data sheet and the surface manufacturer's care guidance. Record the product, its approved surfaces and its use. Do not mix products unless the label and the safety data sheet allow it. Do not let staff choose products from memory.

instruction.heading: Say who supplies what
instruction.body: The sample notes that matting is charged under a separate janitorial contract. Make that kind of split explicit in your own scope. State which party supplies consumables, equipment, replacement parts and any site stock. Also state what the team does about damage, vandalism and security matters. The sample requires graffiti to be reported to security rather than cleaned by the team. Each reporting rule belongs in the scope, with a contact and a timeframe.

instruction.heading: Exclusions and price
instruction.body: Exclusions protect both parties. Name each item that is not included, such as specialist treatments, exterior work, height work or biohazard response, and say whether it can be quoted separately. Then link the scope to hours using the method in the pricing lesson. Every area, frequency and standard in the scope should have a time figure behind it.

procedure: Walk the site and draw a zone map with each area labelled.
List the surfaces, fittings and users of each area.
Write the task list for each area, with one standard per task.
Assign a frequency to every task, using the defined terms.
Write a standard work instruction for each high-use area.
Check each product against the surfaces it will touch, its label, its safety data sheet and the surface guidance.
Write the consumables and equipment responsibility table.
List the exclusions and reporting rules, then estimate hours and price.
Have the client review and sign the scope before the first visit.

workedExamples.situation: An office of three floors has two restrooms, a kitchenette, a lobby, a meeting area and interior glass. The client's draft scope says 'attend to the glass as required' and names no product rules for the stainless-steel sink fittings.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must change in the scope before it is priced, and what belongs in the exclusions?
workedExamples.reasoning: The 'as required' wording is replaced by a defined frequency for interior glass, with a stated response time for spills. The stainless fittings are listed with an approved product, and the scope states that acid-based products are not used on them. Exterior facade work and height work are excluded unless quoted separately, and the business confirms its own competence and licence position before it offers that work.

equipmentAndPpe: Zone map template and clipboard or tablet
Product list with safety data sheet references

commonErrors.prevention: Use defined frequency terms, and write any trigger with a response time.

commonErrors.error: Pricing from a floor plan without a walk
commonErrors.prevention: Walk every area and record surfaces, access and users before writing the hours.
Check the label, the safety data sheet and the surface guidance, and list approved products in the scope.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out exclusions and reporting rules
commonErrors.prevention: Write them into the scope with the contact and the timeframe.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Use acid-based products only on surfaces that the product label, safety data sheet and surface guidance approve, and with the PPE the safety data sheet lists. Check the chemical-use and workplace safety rules that apply in the state or territory where the work is done.

Facade work and work at height are high-risk work. Some work at height and some access methods need specific training or licences. These requirements differ between states and territories, so check the rule where the work is done. This lesson does not grant authority for any height or access work. Check the requirements in the window and pressure cleaning courses before offering that work.

Record only the personal information the job needs on a site scope. Keep access codes and keys in a secure record rather than on a posted sheet, and check the privacy rules that apply to the business.

qualityStandard: Each area has a task list, frequency, standard, responsible role and exclusions.
Every frequency uses a defined term, and every trigger has a response time.
Each product in the scope has a safety data sheet and an approved surface list.
The client has signed the scope before the first visit, and posted instructions are current.
documentationEvidence: Signed scope of works with version and date
Standard work instruction sheets with version numbers
Product and safety data sheet register for the site
summary: A scope defines what, where, how often, to what standard, by whom, and what is excluded.
Frequencies must be defined and checkable.
Products are chosen by surface compatibility and the safety data sheet, not by habit.
Exclusions and reporting rules belong in the scope itself.

knowledgeChecks.question: What does a scope of works mainly define?
options: The owner's profit margin and the owner's car, fuel and phone costs for the year
What work is done, where, how often, to what standard, by whom, and what is excluded
The design of the vehicle signage and the colour and font of the uniforms
The business's registration number and the name of the business accountant and bank

knowledgeChecks.question: A scope says 'attend to restrooms as required'. What is the main problem?
options: It is too short and it lacks a colour and a logo to make it clearly visible
It is measured in square metres, not in time and the cost per square metre is high
It is written in capital letters, so the team cannot read it easily
Frequency cannot be checked, so the client and the team cannot confirm completion

knowledgeChecks.question: A stainless steel fitting is to be cleaned, and the only product available is acid-based. What should happen first?
options: Check the label, the safety data sheet and the surface guidance, and choose a product the surface approves
Use it at full strength, then rinse the fitting dry and the client is told about it afterwards
Mix it with a second product to strengthen it and then test it on the fitting before the client sees it
Let the client choose the product and sign one form for all the work done that day
